title: Naturality for one finite-family index
statement: For a positive finite family in the geometric setup, there exists one additive source comparison eK such that, for every index i, there exist a target comparison eCi and a derived arrow Q(K) -> Q(Ci) satisfying the residue homology naturality equation for every chain representative. The comparisons are chosen together; eK is shared by all indices.

proof.text: Construct the derived arrows between the direct images using the coefficient pullback adjunction units and composition of derived direct images. Restrict to U and conjugate by hE and hCi.

Terminal sections of the strictly perfect models are bounded complexes of finite projective modules. Their termwise residue tensors compute derived residue pullback; degree-one homology is the explicit cycle quotient. hp, the immersion k and hw identify the residue fields.

Arbitrary base change and affine-base cohomology identify the derived fibres with fibre coefficient cohomology. Use tau and its pullbacks to trivialize the coefficients. Use the same geometric source comparison for all i and construct target comparisons by these natural identifications, rather than prescribing arbitrary additive equivalences.

Naturality of the preceding comparisons gives the equation for the constructed derived arrow, and the K-flat comparison makes the equation depend only on the derived image of each chain representative.

statement_change.old_statement: For each index i of a positive finite family, there exists a derived arrow from K to C i such that every chain representative inducing that arrow satisfies the stated residue homology naturality equation.
statement_change.what: The fixed-equivalence helpers universally prescribed arbitrary additive equivalences. Take a smooth plane cubic over C, S=W=Spec(C), k=id, L=O, n=1, Xi=X and ui=id. A strictly perfect model has one-dimensional degree-one residue homology. Choose the source comparison linearly and the target comparison by composing it with complex conjugation in a coordinate. The identity geometric pullback would force conj(H(phi)(z))=z. Every derived arrow between these affine perfect models has a chain representative (perfect_affine_map_representative), and its residue homology map is C-linear, so this is impossible. Instead choose the comparisons together, with one source comparison shared by all indices. The upper geometric naturality theorem already has precisely this existential quantification, and its statement is unchanged.
